title: Replicating Processes
statementMd:
A Large Software Company develops its own social network. Analysts have found that during the holidays, major sporting events and other significant events users begin to enter the network more frequently, resulting in great load increase on the infrastructure.

As part of this task, we assume that the social network is $4*n*$ processes running on the $*n*$ servers. All servers are absolutely identical machines, each of which has a volume of RAM of $1$ GB = $1024$ MB $^{(1)}$. Each process takes 100 MB of RAM on the server. At the same time, the needs of maintaining the viability of the server takes about $100$ more megabytes of RAM. Thus, each server may have up to $9$ different processes of social network.

Now each of the $*n*$ servers is running exactly $4$ processes. However, at the moment of peak load it is sometimes necessary to replicate the existing $4*n*$ processes by creating $8*n*$ new processes instead of the old ones. More formally, there is a set of replication rules, the $*i*$-th ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ 4*n*$) of which has the form of $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$, where $*a*_{*i*}$, $*b*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) are the numbers of servers. This means that instead of an old process running on server $*a*_{*i*}$, there should appear two new copies of the process running on servers $*b*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$. The two new replicated processes can be on the same server (i.e., $*b*_{*i*}$ may be equal to $*c*_{*i*}$) or even on the same server where the original process was (i.e. $*a*_{*i*}$ may be equal to $*b*_{*i*}$ or $*c*_{*i*}$). During the implementation of the rule $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$ first the process from the server $*a*_{*i*}$ is destroyed, then appears a process on the server $*b*_{*i*}$, then appears a process on the server $*c*_{*i*}$.

There is a set of $4*n*$ rules, destroying all the original $4*n*$ processes from $*n*$ servers, and creating after their application $8*n*$ replicated processes, besides, on each of the $*n*$ servers will be exactly $8$ processes. However, the rules can only be applied consecutively, and therefore the amount of RAM of the servers imposes limitations on the procedure for the application of the rules.

According to this set of rules determine the order in which you want to apply all the $4*n*$ rules so that at any given time the memory of each of the servers contained at most $9$ processes (old and new together), or tell that it is impossible.

## Input

The first line of the input contains integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 30 000$) — the number of servers of the social network.

Next $4*n*$ lines contain the rules of replicating processes, the $*i*$-th ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ 4*n*$) of these lines as form $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) and describes rule $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$.

It is guaranteed that each number of a server from $1$ to $*n*$ occurs four times in the set of all $*a*_{*i*}$, and eight times among a set that unites all $*b*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$.

## Output

If the required order of performing rules does not exist, print "`NO`" (without the quotes).

Otherwise, print in the first line "`YES`" (without the quotes), and in the second line — a sequence of $4*n*$ numbers from $1$ to $4*n*$, giving the numbers of the rules in the order they are applied. The sequence should be a permutation, that is, include each number from $1$ to $4*n*$ exactly once.

If there are multiple possible variants, you are allowed to print any of them.

## Note

$^{(1)}$ To be extremely accurate, we should note that the amount of server memory is $1$ GiB = $1024$ MiB and processes require $100$ MiB RAM where a gibibyte (GiB) is the amount of RAM of $2^{30}$ bytes and a mebibyte (MiB) is the amount of RAM of $2^{20}$ bytes.

In the first sample test the network uses two servers, each of which initially has four launched processes. In accordance with the rules of replication, each of the processes must be destroyed and twice run on another server. One of the possible answers is given in the statement: after applying rules $1$ and $2$ the first server will have $2$ old running processes, and the second server will have $8$ ($4$ old and $4$ new) processes. After we apply rules $5$ and $6$, both servers will have $6$ running processes ($2$ old and $4$ new). After we apply rules $3$ and $7$, both servers will have $7$ running processes ($1$ old and $6$ new), and after we apply rules $4$ and $8$, each server will have $8$ running processes. At no time the number of processes on a single server exceeds $9$.

In the second sample test the network uses three servers. On each server, three processes are replicated into two processes on the same server, and the fourth one is replicated in one process for each of the two remaining servers. As a result of applying rules $2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12$ each server would have $7$ processes ($6$ old and $1$ new), as a result of applying rules $1, 5, 9$ each server will have $8$ processes. At no time the number of processes on a single server exceeds $9$.
statementZhMd:
大型软件公司开发了自己的社交网络。分析人员发现，在节假日、重大体育赛事以及其他重要事件期间，用户开始更加频繁地访问网络，从而导致基础设施负载大幅增加。

在本题中，我们假设社交网络由运行在 $*n*$ 台服务器上的 $4*n*$ 个进程组成。所有服务器都是完全相同的机器，每台服务器的 RAM 容量为 $1$ GB = $1024$ MB $^{(1)}$。每个进程在服务器上占用 100 MB RAM。同时，维持服务器正常运行还需要占用约 $100$ MB RAM。因此，每台服务器最多可以运行 $9$ 个不同的社交网络进程。

现在，$*n*$ 台服务器中的每台都恰好运行着 $4$ 个进程。然而，在负载高峰期，有时需要通过创建 $8*n*$ 个新进程来复制已有的 $4*n*$ 个进程，并替代旧进程。更形式化地说，有一组复制规则，其中第 $*i*$ 条（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ 4*n*$）规则的形式为 $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$，其中 $*a*_{*i*}$、$*b*_{*i*}$ 和 $*c*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$）表示服务器编号。这意味着，应当销毁运行在服务器 $*a*_{*i*}$ 上的旧进程，并在服务器 $*b*_{*i*}$ 和 $*c*_{*i*}$ 上分别创建该进程的两个新副本。这两个新复制出的进程可以位于同一台服务器上（即 $*b*_{*i*}$ 可能等于 $*c*_{*i*}$），甚至可以位于原进程所在的同一台服务器上（即 $*a*_{*i*}$ 可能等于 $*b*_{*i*}$ 或 $*c*_{*i*}$）。执行规则 $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$ 时，首先销毁服务器 $*a*_{*i*}$ 上的进程，然后在服务器 $*b*_{*i*}$ 上创建一个进程，最后在服务器 $*c*_{*i*}$ 上创建一个进程。

给定一组共 $4*n*$ 条规则，它们会销毁 $*n*$ 台服务器上的全部 $4*n*$ 个初始进程，并在执行完所有规则后创建 $8*n*$ 个复制进程；此外，最终每台服务器上都恰好有 $8$ 个进程。然而，由于规则只能依次执行，因此服务器的 RAM 容量会限制规则的执行过程。

请根据给定的规则，确定执行全部 $4*n*$ 条规则的顺序，使得在任意时刻，每台服务器上包含的进程数（旧进程和新进程总数）都不超过 $9$；如果无法做到，则说明不可能。

## 输入

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 30 000$）——社交网络中的服务器数量。

接下来 $4*n*$ 行包含复制进程的规则，第 $*i*$ 条（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ 4*n*$）的格式为 $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$），表示规则 $*a*_{*i*} → (*b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*})$。

保证服务器编号 $1$ 到 $*n*$ 中的每个数字，在所有 $*a*_{*i*}$ 组成的集合中恰好出现四次，并且在由所有 $*b*_{*i*}$ 和 $*c*_{*i*}$ 合并而成的集合中出现八次。

## 输出

如果不存在满足要求的规则执行顺序，输出 `` `NO` ``（不含引号）。

否则，第一行输出 `` `YES` ``（不含引号），第二行输出 $4*n*$ 个从 $1$ 到 $4*n*$ 的数字，表示规则的执行顺序。该序列必须是一个排列，即每个从 $1$ 到 $4*n*$ 的数字都恰好出现一次。

如果有多个可行方案，可以输出任意一种。

## 说明

$^{(1)}$ 更严谨地说，服务器的内存容量为 $1$ GiB = $1024$ MiB，而进程需要 $100$ MiB RAM，其中 GiB（gibibyte）表示 $2^{30}$ 字节的 RAM 容量，MiB（mebibyte）表示 $2^{20}$ 字节的 RAM 容量。

在第一个样例中，网络使用两台服务器，每台服务器最初运行着四个进程。根据复制规则，每个进程都必须被销毁，并在另一台服务器上运行两个副本。题面中给出了一种可能的答案：执行规则 $1$ 和 $2$ 后，第一台服务器上有 $2$ 个旧进程，第二台服务器上有 $8$ 个进程（$4$ 个旧进程和 $4$ 个新进程）。执行规则 $5$ 和 $6$ 后，两台服务器上都有 $6$ 个运行中的进程（$2$ 个旧进程和 $4$ 个新进程）。执行规则 $3$ 和 $7$ 后，两台服务器上都有 $7$ 个运行中的进程（$1$ 个旧进程和 $6$ 个新进程）；执行规则 $4$ 和 $8$ 后，每台服务器上都有 $8$ 个运行中的进程。在任何时刻，单台服务器上的进程数都不会超过 $9$。

在第二个样例中，网络使用三台服务器。每台服务器上有三个进程被复制为位于同一台服务器上的两个进程，第四个进程则分别在另外两台服务器上各复制出一个进程。执行规则 $2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12$ 后，每台服务器上都有 $7$ 个进程（$6$ 个旧进程和 $1$ 个新进程）；执行规则 $1, 5, 9$ 后，每台服务器上都有 $8$ 个进程。在任何时刻，单台服务器上的进程数都不会超过 $9$。
